messages:
tess (pm): quick sync 1: we need to finalize the abort/rollback model for long apply-windows in the onprem packaging RFC. there are a few operator painpoints in the runbook drafts. ideas?

ian (eng-arch): main question: operator-facing action = 'pause' vs 'abort'. pause should be a safe no-op for serving, abort must guarantee a well-defined revert path. also need an immutable activation marker so we can reason about partial rollouts.

rohit (eng-infra): infra prefers three primitives: 1) commit checkpoint at shard boundary, 2) signed tombstone for a paused shard, 3) abort-to-previous manifest that triggers snapshot restore. tying actions to shard.commit sequence makes GC simpler.

morgan (operator): practical ops: when an apply stalls mid-shard we want a fast-abort that flips shard to QUARANTINE (prevent serving reads) and emits an invalidate event. QUARANTINE -> either RESUME or ROLLBACK. needs to be visible in console.

anya (security): security: any state transition (PAUSE/QUARANTINE/ROLLBACK/COMMIT) must be recorded in an append-only ledger entry signed by the actor. ledger entries are the source-of-truth for the verifier. no silent state.

ian (eng-arch): ledger entry fields proposal: seq, shard_id, manifest_id, prev_seq, state, actor, reason, ts, sig_alg, sig_blob. seq is monotonic per-manifest. we also add a `marker_type` where tombstones and quarantines are explicit.

rohit (eng-infra): storage: ledger entries as CBOR small objects colocated with manifest index. replication: replicated to controllers so offline operators can still read state. for private installs, allow operator-local signing but mark sig_alg="local" in ledger.

leah (devex): console UX: show shard timeline inline with ledger entries. collapsible by component. for abort flow show a preview of affected serving prefixes and an estimated blast radius. also add a "fast-abort" button that creates a QUARANTINE entry and a separate "rollback" confirmation that executes snapshot restore or reverse-apply.

morgan (operator): yes to preview. other ask: CLI must support dry-run and produce the actual signed ledger blob so oncall can paste into audit tickets. example: `redwoodctl activation fast-abort --manifest m-2026-06-01 --shard sh-09 --reason "bad checksum" --dry-run`.

ian (eng-arch): for invalidation: serving-plane contract = on invalidate event publish (manifest, seq, action, ttl, nonce, sig). serving nodes validate sig + seq monotonicity before evicting prefixes. we should include an ack path so controllers know when a node has processed invalidation.

anya (security): tokens: use HMAC-SHA256 with per-customer KMS key. token includes nonce=(manifest,seq,random), ttl=60s. nodes cache seen nonces for ttl to prevent replay. ledger entry references token hash for audit.

rohit (eng-infra): regarding rollback strategies: manifest shard metadata can include `rollback: {strategy: "reverse"|"snapshot", min_snapshot_size: <bytes>, snapshot_ref: "..."}`. default: reverse for <10MB, snapshot otherwise. snapshots are content-addressed and signed.

morgan (operator): operational nuance: reverse-apply may fail if a transform was non-idempotent. prefer snapshot for model blobs. we should warn operators in console which shards are snapshot-only.

leah (devex): add sample redwoodctl output to docs. small example in-line: 
``
$ redwoodctl activation fast-abort --manifest m-2026-06-01 --shard sh-09 --reason "bad checksum"
DRY-RUN: would write LEDGER ENTRY: seq=128 shard=sh-09 state=QUARANTINE actor=operator:morgan ts=1805001234 sig_type=local
PREVIEW: would invalidate ~12 prefixes on routes: /models/xxx, /cache/yyy
```

rohit (eng-infra): file atomicity: writers use temp suffix `.write.<seq>` then atomic rename. if QUARANTINE occurs mid-write, installer leaves temp intact and ledger records it. GC removes stale temps older than configurable threshold (default 24h). reclaimed temps must be included in GC audit logs.

anya (security): audit rules: archive all signed ledger entries (hot store can be GC'd) into immutable object storage for compliance window (default 1y for enterprise). ledger entries must record signer key id and algorithm, and if an offline key was used the `sig_provenance` freeform must explain reason.

ian (eng-arch): edge-case: partial commit across shards (some shards COMMITTED, others QUARANTINED). allow eventual consistency: serving can serve committed shards, but activation is only "fully active" once all shards COMMITTED. verifier checks per-shard ledger chain. manifest status endpoint should show partial progress and overall activation state.

morgan (operator): runbook item: sequence to abort and recover: 1) fast-abort -> QUARANTINE ledger entry, 2) console preview and confirm rollback, 3a) if snapshot strategy -> trigger snapshot-restore job, 3b) if reverse -> run reverse-apply with validation, 4) post-rollback commit ledger entry, 5) emit invalidate token to serving. include commands for each step in RFC.

leah (devex): i'll draft the runbook snippet and a console mock with the collapsible shard timeline. want to show the signed tombstone JSON for novices.

ian (eng-arch): action items for RFC patch:
- formal ledger schema + CBOR storage + archive rules (ian + anya)
- manifest shard rollback metadata + default heuristics (rohit)
- file write atomicity + temp-file GC + GC audit (rohit)
- console + cli fast-abort, preview, dry-run examples (leah + morgan)
- invalidate token spec + serving ack semantics + nonce replay protection (anya)
- runbook example with exact `redwoodctl` commands (morgan)

tess (pm): solid. i'll take these and make a follow-up RFC patch. aim to PR by Monday. any objections?

deploy-bot: queued rfc/onprem-packaging-abort-ux patch -> staging (id: d-6021)

ian (eng-arch): no objections, thanks. one last ask: include metrics we should emit (abort_count, quarantine_count, rollback_duration, invalidate_latency) so SRE can alert.

rohit (eng-infra): noted, will add metrics.

morgan (operator): thanks all. adding the runbook to my checklist.

tess (pm): thanks everyone — i'll ping when PR is up. :)
